newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-MALCOLM AND CONNOR LAUNCH CHAMPIONSHIP IN STYLE.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-MALCOLM AND CONNOR LAUNCH CHAMPIONSHIP IN STYLE.

text.p: England discard Devon Malcolm and fellow West Indian-born paceman Cardigan Connor seized six and seven wickets respectively in a compelling start to the English county championship season on Wednesday.

Lancashire middle order batsman Graham Lloyd blasted a century off 78 deliveries and the county's last-wicket pair of Peter Martin and Glen Chapple shared an unbroken stand of 134 as bowlers did not have it all their way on the first day of four-day matches.
Malcolm, overlooked by England since his unhappy tour of South Africa in 1995-96, took an early chance to impress new chairman of selectors David Graveney at Canterbury.
His six for 74 in 27 overs enabled Derbyshire, last season's championship runners-up, to dismiss Kent for 251 on a hard and bouncy pitch.
However, Martin McCague, another ex-England fast bowler, hit back with three for 14 to have Derbyshire reeling on 35 for four at the close.
Connor, in his 14th season with Hampshire, rocked Essex at Chelmsford with the fourth best performance of his career - seven for 46 to send the home county crashing from 129 for one to 246 all out.
Essex, fired by four for 35 from seamer Ashley Cowan, fought back by reducing Hampshire to 103 for seven at the close.
Lancashire gave Durham's new captain-manager, former Australian test batsman David Boon, a harsh welcome to county cricket as they piled up 494 for nine at Old Trafford.
Lloyd, son of England coach David, hammered 102, including 19 fours, to follow his 225 off 151 balls against Yorkshire in a pre-season friendly.
Just when Durham thought their day of toil was over at 360 for nine, Chapple (65 not out) and Martin (67 not out) completed a century partnership in 15 overs.
Chapple got his half-century off 62 balls and Martin reached his 50 off 45 deliveries, their stand of 134 being the second highest for Lancashire's 10th wicket this century.
England left-arm seamer Alan Mullally took five for 52 as champions Leicestershire were held up by middle order resistance from Gloucestershire at Leicester.

Gloucestershire slipped to 84 for five before new Tasmanian signing Shaun Young hit their top score of 59 and, with England wicketkeeper Jack Russell (57), led a revival to 245 all out. The title holders were 99 for three at the close.
